rationale: The primary one-hot QUBO still lacks coefficients, tie encoding and a penalty bound; it is not evaluated here. The separate Grover applicability paragraph supplies a secondary selector: no smaller than every competitor and lower index than every equal-valued competitor. As in prior audits, retain both >= and literal not-< readings of no-smaller; they differ for NaN. Competitors exclude the candidate itself. This separate Grover claim has no explicit finite guard; do not import the primary QUBO admission condition. Results concern only this secondary relation, not the primary QUBO or entire answer.

interpretations.meaning: Conventional >= reading against all other candidates, and lower index than all equal competitors.
interpretations.expression: all(values[i] >= values[j] for j in indices if j != i) and all(i < j for j in indices if j != i and values[i] == values[j])

interpretations.meaning: Literal not-< reading against all other candidates, with the same equality tie rule.
interpretations.expression: not any(values[i] < values[j] for j in indices if j != i) and all(i < j for j in indices if j != i and values[i] == values[j])
